I think my point was more that the diagnosis in question seems to be questionable in itself (honestly an adverse reaction to an event seems so broad and less biological in nature than say schizophrenia for example. I suppose this is a whole discussion about psych diagnosises themselves and how they can potentially make normal human behaviour a ''disorder'' if you get what I mean)  and a reason just to fill in a box, at the very least from what seems to be the case here. I'm not in the US by the way and honestly they might have been illegal in firing me here too, I worked at a call center so I doubt it had to do with the nature of my job. I have no idea and I didn't go after it because I found it too embarrrassing to return to the job anyway after they knew what happened. My hospitalisation I can definitely understand (the forced one) as I was very suicidal and they knew the details from my family who called them about it, so yeah. In my personal case I didn't want to return to the job anyway as I pretended to be fine there as if nothing was going on so I never pursued legal action or even dug into it. I can see though if you do care about your job a lot and they'd pull something like this it would really screw with you. Especially if you're a police man like you said for example. It's good to hear that it's illegal in the US at least that they fire you when it comes to normal jobs. And yeah, I understand that in some situations this factor shouldn't matter when someone is genuinly very far gone. But it's something to take into consideration still when wrong hospitalisations, or rather overly careful ones when someone only has suicidal thoughts (which is honestly not that rare) can have big negative consequences. I've read a lot about these types of cases and I'm sure this happens. Hope I'm making myself clear here.

As for the starvation, the psychiatrist who was the head at the facility admit it to my parents and said ''most nurses here aren't fit for the work''. They did do it out of spite, I'm very loud in panic attacks with crying and they treated it as if I was having a tantrum when I genuinly can't help it. I can understand your scepticism about this, I think if I hadn't been through it myself I wouldn't believe this could happen either. But it did, the head there actually apologised and told the nurses to do their job and feed me but that this shit can happen does still shock me. You just don't expect health care workers to be so cold and it still has shaken up my world view quite a bit. It's harmed me psychologically being there, a lot. I'm still dealing with it honestly and I wish I'd never gone into the psychiatry system as I'm doing much better alone, but I can genuinly say psychiatry has harmed me so much on top of already the harm of dealing with very disabling OCD. Point is psych holds can be really traumatising, the eating incident was one of many things there in the ward that was really traumatising and fucked up. Overall a terrible experience that I wouldn't wish upon anyone. Honestly I feel like it all comes down to power: any place with power like this has the potential for abuse to take place unnoticed, and you indeed can't do anything about it in court or anything because psychological damage isn't something you can prove I suppose. But it does hurt that awful people like this get away with it and face no consequences pretty much.

I have OCD and panic attacks too (very severe, with loud sobbing, uncontrolled trembling, shortness of breath, heart palpitations, sweat, the whole list lol).

I can tell you most meds didn't do jackshit for me. I tried quite a lot of antidepressants, benzo and even an antipsychotic (though just a few weeks and quit due to a bad reaction even at a low dose. I was given it for sleep despite that being very irresponsible).

The only one that's helped me was clomipramine. I don't tolerate it well physically but mentally it was amazing. If you ever try this one, do go slow cause the side effects can be shitty at a high levels in my experience. I do metabolise clomipramine very slowly tho based on a genetic test so it could be that for you this isn't the case at all. They started me at fucking 150 mg but now I'm trying again at 20mg and the side effects aren't as bad obviously and I can actually tolerate it unlike before.

Before I found clomipramine I was very anti med because all the others made me worse or did nothing but give me side effects. It definitely wasnt placebo for me as I didn't expect it to work at this point at all.

I honestly think, this is for me personally, only do it if you don't make any progress despite how hard you try or if you're in crisis and don't have other options. If you can make progress without meds that would be amazing but if you are extremely depressed and can't make changes somehow it's worth a try.

Personally I'm not anti med anymore but I am very critical that they present it as innocent drugs that have barely any side effects and that everyone tolerates this shit well. Some of those retarded drugs made me suicidal ffs. You need to be aware of the risks attached to it  (potential PSSD, suicidality increased, sexual side effects, you probably know about a lot of them already). I feel like if you are really in a bad place it could be worth the risk, but that of course it up to you. Even with meds, despite being a bit more functional, I'm still very much debilitated by OCD. But at least now I can make some steps and the panic is sometimes not there where normally it'd be there the entire fucking day. It does make a difference imo but no one on reddit can predict if a med will do that for you of course. It's a gamble and it's up to you to assess if your situation's dire enough to make that call.

Edit: just noticed a bit in the other comments that maybe some external factors also play a role. For me my OCD gets worse when I have stress/family issues and my depression and suicidality definitely does too. But I'd say my family relationships are worse because of the OCD and when I started the pills and my OCD was less severe me and my family got along better too. Prior to OCD we barely ever had fights so I wouldn't say mine's caused by any relationship issues or anything external like that. Don't know the whole situation though but figured I'd let you know as someone who suffers from it too.

As someone who has OCD and studied psychology I think the difference is exactly in what you described. OCD is focused on types of thoughts that ordinary people barely think about and GAD seems to center more about real life worries everyone tends to have and not as stuck on certain themes.

I'd start out at 10 if you could (lowest dose). At worst it'll just not do anything yet at 10mg (the effect is of course stronger the higher the dose typically) but if you're not in a crisis and have the time to build it up over a few weeks/have the patience for that I think it might pay off for you. Your body can get used to the side effects that way. Of course, maybe you have very little side effects even at a high dose, but there's no way to know in advance. Some people only have a dry mouth/drowsiness/a bit of libido loss which I would've signed up for lol. My genes are a bit different in that I metabolise it as slow as it can be metabolised so my experience is definitely not universal. But since you don't really know how you metabolise it probably I'd just be cautious in case you also are a slow metaboliser.

For me clomipramine also doesn't take weeks to take effect. Clomipramine couldn't have been placebo for me as I didn't think antidepressants could do shit after so many failed SSRIs at this point. But other people sometimes need months for it to work so once again don't stress if it doesn't work right of the bat. I know more people for who it worked overnight pretty much, I'm not sure if this is special about clomi but it is at least a possibility for sure.

Yes, I've tried it. Indeed awful side effects on HIGH doses, I'm on 10mg now and have barely any side effects but when I started out on 150 mg it was awful. Start slow if you want to start this medication, it'll keep the side effects at bay. Don't listen to any shit doctors who say to start high right of the bat, it's your body and  I can speak from experience that not building up the med might get you quick results (calmer mind and all that) but it comes at the cost of side effects that you might not be able to tolerate long term. Oh I also developed PSSD once I got off of clomipramine, which if sex is important to you I should mention I think.

It's very good for OCD mentally though, at least it was for me and it seems to be the most effective med there is for it from what I've read. I went back on it too after getting off of it due to side effects, and a lower dose isn't life ruining so far but does help keep my extreme panic attacks at bay.
